title: Subsets
corePattern: Power Set Enumeration via Backtracking and Bitmasking
interviewTips: Clarify constraints: Are all numbers distinct? Problem guarantees distinct integers, so no duplicate-subset handling needed unlike Subsets II.
Trade-off: Backtracking vs Iterative vs Bitmask all cost O(2^n * n) time; choose backtracking for interview clarity, iterative for simplicity, bitmask for direct index-to-subset mapping.
Edge-case tip: Empty input must return [[]] not [], and emphasize output size is 2^n — discuss why exponential output dominates complexity analysis.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Backtracking (DFS Include-or-Explore)
approaches.intuition: Each element has two choices: include it or skip it. Do a depth-first search that builds a current path, records it as a valid subset, then tries adding each remaining element one by one and recurses.
approaches.theory: We maintain start index to avoid revisiting earlier elements and generating permutations. At each call we add a copy of path to answer (all lengths are valid). Then for i from start to n-1 we push nums[i], recurse with i+1, and pop to backtrack. This enumerates the full decision tree with exactly 2^n nodes, each node corresponds to one subset.

timeComplexity.explanation: There are 2^n subsets. Copying each path of average length n/2 costs O(n), so total O(2^n * n). Recursion visits each subset once.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Output stores 2^n subsets totaling O(2^n * n) integers. Auxiliary space is O(n) for recursion depth and path, plus O(2^n * n) for answer.

edgeCases: Negative numbers work identically, no sorting needed

approaches.name: Approach 2: Iterative Cascading (Optimal)
approaches.intuition: Start with only the empty set. For each new number, duplicate all existing subsets and append the number to the copies. This cascades the power set size from 1 to 2 to 4 to 8.
approaches.theory: Invariant: after processing first k numbers, res contains all 2^k subsets of nums[0..k-1]. When processing nums[k], every subset of first k+1 elements either excludes nums[k] (already in res) or includes it (existing subset + nums[k]). So we snapshot size n=res.size() and for i in 0..n-1 push copy with new element. No recursion needed.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each of n iterations doubles list: total copies sum_{k} 2^k = 2^{n+1}. Each copy costs O(k) average, bounded by O(2^n * n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Output dominates. Auxiliary extra is O(1) besides output if we count copying cost as output construction; iterative uses no recursion stack.

edgeCases: Must snapshot n=res.size() before inner loop or infinite growth

approaches.name: Approach 3: Bit Manipulation (Bitmask Enumeration)
approaches.intuition: Number subsets from 0 to 2^n -1. Write the number in binary: bit i = 1 means include nums[i]. Each mask directly encodes one subset.
approaches.theory: There is a bijection between n-bit integers and subsets of an n-element set. For mask in [0, 2^n), subset = {nums[i] | mask & (1<<i) != 0}. Iterate all masks and build subsets by testing bits. n <= 10 per constraints so 1<<n fits in int; for larger n use 1LL or iterative method.

timeComplexity.explanation: 2^n masks, each scans n bits to build subset, so O(n * 2^n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Output storage dominates. Extra working space O(n) per subset built temporarily.

edgeCases: For n>=31 shift overflows int, need long or backtracking
